content: Ceftolozane/tazobactam is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections. It is administered intravenously, typically every 8 hours, and should be infused slowly over one hour. The dosage is determined based on the patient’s medical condition and response to treatment. If used at home, patients must be trained on proper preparation and administration techniques. Before use, the solution should be inspected for particles or discoloration, and any abnormalities should prompt disposal of the product. Common side effects include pain, redness, or irritation at the injection site, as well as nausea, diarrhea, or headache. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during or even weeks to months after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or new yeast infections. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. Patients should immediately report any severe symptoms, such as difficulty breathing or swelling. Before starting ceftolozane/tazobactam, patients should inform their healthcare provider if they have allergies to cephalosporins, penicillins, or other antibiotics, or if they have any other allergies. This medication contains sodium and may interfere with live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine, reducing their effectiveness. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as its effects on fetal development are not well established. It is also unknown if the drug passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding mothers should consult their doctor. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of ceftolozane/tazobactam or increase the risk of side effects. Patients should provide their healthcare provider with a complete list of all medications and supplements they are taking. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine glucose tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose, individuals experiencing severe symptoms, such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, should seek emergency medical attention immediately by calling 911. For non-emergency situations, contact a poison control center. Proper storage of the medication is crucial. Unreconstituted vials should be refrigerated at 2–8°C (36–46°F) and protected from light. Reconstituted vials can remain at room temperature for up to one hour before being transferred and diluted in an infusion bag. Once diluted, the solution is stable for 24 hours at room temperature or up to 7 days if refrigerated. Freezing the solution is not recommended. Expired or unused medication should be discarded appropriately, following the guidance of a pharmacist or local disposal regulations. Patients should attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments to monitor their response to treatment and assess for potential side effects. If a dose is missed, patients should contact their healthcare provider promptly for instructions on rescheduling. This medication should not be flushed down the toilet or poured into a drain unless specifically instructed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about ceftolozane/tazobactam. Patients should always consult their healthcare provider for personalized medical advice and complete information about their treatment.
